statement: For bounded complexes of finite-length modules, alternating total length is additive and equals alternating cohomology length. For a coherent sheaf on a projective scheme over an artinian base, the Euler characteristic of its twists is a polynomial for all integers and agrees with the length of global sections for sufficiently large twists; its leading coefficient is positive when the sheaf is nonzero.
reconstruction: Positivity does not mean every coefficient is positive. The zero sheaf gives the zero polynomial; strict inequalities require the nonzero hypothesis.
check_reason: The proof of Euler additivity is present; the Hilbert-polynomial context is partially carried over from reused paper.

statement: For a flat ring map A→B, faithfulness is equivalent to nonvanishing after tensoring every nonzero A-module, to surjectivity Spec B→Spec A, and to proper extension of every maximal ideal; faithful flatness gives contraction IB∩A=I and injective tensor-unit maps.
reconstruction: The displayed B h(A) must be compared to the quotient B/h(A) used in the following proof; this is a likely slash omission. Flatness is indispensable in the equivalence package.
check_reason: The proof and the surrounding equivalent conditions were read rather than inferred from the heading.

statement: On a paracompact Hausdorff space, softness of a suitable sheaf of rings supports partitions of unity subordinate to locally finite covers; the local softness condition requires extension from closed sets and is not satisfied by every constant sheaf.
reconstruction: The proof is partial and uses a maximal-family extension. The exact support and paracompactness assumptions must remain explicit.
check_reason: Both the partition argument and the local definition/counterexample context were read.

statement: The reused sheaf-theory text embeds any sheaf of abelian groups F into F⊗I, where I is the sheaf of arbitrary integer-valued functions, and uses I-module structure to obtain a fine sheaf. At each stalk evaluation at the base point splits Z→I_x, so the tensor-unit map is injective.
reconstruction: The stalkwise retraction is the earlier run’s alternative proof; it does not furnish one global evaluation map. Open/closed extension statements require their own standard sheaf-theoretic hypotheses.
check_reason: The embedding is written; the stronger global splitting is not. The two entries are merged as statement and proof audit.
